variants.headline: Party leader faces a public scandal
variants.sub: A party leader is the subject of a newly revealed scandal.
variants.body:
A scandal about a party leader has come to light. The revelation makes political trust an immediate subject of public attention. An assessment of {target} must distinguish that known fact from unreported details about the conduct involved, its cause or any proceedings that might follow.

Our political principles ought to survive the discomfort of applying them to leaders. Trust is not a private asset belonging to a party hierarchy. It concerns the people asked to give their support, and they deserve an argument about responsibility that does not depend on convenient invention.

This paper treats {target} as a subject for scrutiny, while withholding conclusions the reported revelation does not establish. Attention to trust need not depend upon an invented account of wrongdoing. Political principle should remain visible when judgment becomes less comfortable.

variants.headline: Leadership under an unwelcome spotlight
variants.sub: A scandal about a party leader has become public in the colony.
variants.body:

variants.headline: A scandal tests political trust
variants.sub: A scandal concerning a party leader has come to light in {colony}.
variants.body:
